collections.title: LLM & AI Research
collections.subtitle: Foundations, block anatomy, alignment, systems, reasoning, frontier architectures

items.title: Attention Is All You Need
items.why: Transformer foundation: self-attention, MHA, positional encoding.
items.exercise: Implement scaled dot-product + multi-head attention.

items.title: Improving Language Understanding by Generative Pre-Training
items.why: Generative pretraining followed by task adaptation; start of the GPT line.
items.exercise: Train a tiny causal LM, then fine-tune it on a toy task.

items.title: BERT: Pre-training of Deep Bidirectional Transformers for Language Understanding
items.why: Canonical encoder-only masked-language-model pretraining; useful contrast with GPT.
items.exercise: Implement masked-LM training on a tiny encoder.

items.title: Language Models are Unsupervised Multitask Learners
items.why: Major step toward zero-shot task transfer with scaled decoder-only LMs.
items.exercise: Compare zero-shot prompts across a few small tasks.

items.title: Language Models are Few-Shot Learners
items.why: Established in-context few-shot learning as a central LLM capability.
items.exercise: Reproduce zero-shot vs few-shot prompting on an open model.

items.title: Scaling Laws for Neural Language Models
items.why: Empirical power-law relationships among loss, model size, data and compute.
items.exercise: Fit a simple power-law curve to small-model training runs.

items.title: Training Compute-Optimal Large Language Models
items.why: Shows why many large models were undertrained on data; compute-optimal scaling.
items.exercise: Build a compute-optimal parameter/token calculator.

items.title: The Pile: An 800GB Dataset of Diverse Text for Language Modeling
items.why: Large-scale pretraining data composition, diversity and dataset design.
items.exercise: Inspect mixture proportions and design a small balanced corpus.

items.title: PaLM: Scaling Language Modeling with Pathways
items.why: Major dense-model scaling report with systems and reasoning observations.
items.exercise: Map parameters, tokens, accelerators, parallelism and evaluations.

items.title: OPT: Open Pre-trained Transformer Language Models
items.why: Especially valuable for openness, training logs and reproducibility lessons.
items.exercise: Summarize infrastructure failures and recovery lessons from the logbook.

items.title: BLOOM: A 176B-Parameter Open-Access Multilingual Language Model
items.why: Open multilingual LLM project with unusually transparent data/training collaboration.
items.exercise: Compare BLOOM's data/model choices with OPT and LLaMA.

items.title: LLaMA: Open and Efficient Foundation Language Models
items.why: Influential compact modern decoder-only recipe; key bridge to current open LLMs.
items.exercise: Implement a LLaMA-style block with RMSNorm, SwiGLU and RoPE.

items.title: Root Mean Square Layer Normalization
items.why: Explains the normalization variant widely used in modern LLMs.
items.exercise: Compare LayerNorm vs RMSNorm numerically and by runtime.

items.title: GLU Variants Improve Transformer
items.why: Basis for SwiGLU/GLU feed-forward blocks in many modern LLMs.
items.exercise: Implement ReLU/GELU/GLU/SwiGLU and compare FLOPs/parameters.

items.title: RoFormer: Enhanced Transformer with Rotary Position Embedding
items.why: Introduces rotary positional embeddings, central to modern decoder-only models.
items.exercise: Implement RoPE and visualize query/key rotations vs distance.

items.title: Train Short, Test Long: Attention with Linear Biases Enables Input Length Extrapolation
items.why: Simple positional-bias alternative; useful contrast with RoPE.
items.exercise: Add ALiBi to attention and test length extrapolation.

items.title: Fast Transformer Decoding: One Write-Head is All You Need
items.why: Why sharing K/V heads reduces bandwidth and KV-cache cost during decoding.
items.exercise: Calculate and benchmark KV-cache size for MHA vs MQA.

items.title: GQA: Training Generalized Multi-Query Transformer Models from Multi-Head Checkpoints
items.why: Quality/efficiency middle ground between MHA and MQA used by many modern LLMs.
items.exercise: Implement GQA; compare cache size and decode latency.

items.title: Training Language Models to Follow Instructions with Human Feedback
items.why: Canonical RLHF pipeline: SFT, reward modeling and policy optimization.
items.exercise: Sketch or implement a toy SFT → preference model → policy pipeline.

items.title: Constitutional AI: Harmlessness from AI Feedback
items.why: Introduces self-critique/revision and RLAIF-style alignment from written principles.
items.exercise: Build a small critique-revision loop with explicit rules.

items.title: Self-Instruct: Aligning Language Models with Self-Generated Instructions
items.why: Shows how synthetic instructions can bootstrap instruction-following data.
items.exercise: Generate, filter and deduplicate a small synthetic instruction set.

items.title: LoRA: Low-Rank Adaptation of Large Language Models
items.why: Foundational low-rank parameter-efficient fine-tuning method.
items.exercise: Implement a LoRA linear layer and verify merged/unmerged outputs.

items.title: QLoRA: Efficient Finetuning of Quantized LLMs
items.why: Combines 4-bit quantization with LoRA for very memory-efficient fine-tuning.
items.exercise: Fine-tune a small model in 4-bit + LoRA and record memory use.

items.title: Direct Preference Optimization: Your Language Model is Secretly a Reward Model
items.why: Influential preference objective that avoids a separate RL reward-model loop.
items.exercise: Derive and implement the DPO loss on toy preference pairs.

items.title: ORPO: Monolithic Preference Optimization without Reference Model
items.why: Reference-model-free preference method; good comparison against DPO/GRPO.
items.exercise: Compare ORPO and DPO objectives on the same toy dataset.

items.title: Megatron-LM: Training Multi-Billion Parameter Language Models Using Model Parallelism
items.why: Foundational tensor-model-parallel training paper; key ML↔distributed-systems bridge.
items.exercise: Work through tensor-parallel sharding and communication volume.

items.title: ZeRO: Memory Optimizations Toward Training Trillion Parameter Models
items.why: Essential memory accounting for parameters, gradients and optimizer states.
items.exercise: Build a memory calculator for ZeRO stages 1/2/3.

items.title: FlashAttention: Fast and Memory-Efficient Exact Attention with IO-Awareness
items.why: Reframes attention performance around GPU memory traffic and IO complexity.
items.exercise: Benchmark naive vs tiled attention; reason about HBM↔SRAM traffic.

items.title: FlashAttention-2: Faster Attention with Better Parallelism and Work Partitioning
items.why: Improves work partitioning and parallelism to raise GPU utilization.
items.exercise: Study warp/block work partitioning and occupancy bottlenecks.

items.title: FlashAttention-3: Fast and Accurate Attention with Asynchrony and Low-precision
items.why: Outstanding hardware-aware paper on Hopper, TMA, warp specialization and FP8.
items.exercise: Map the H100 pipeline and where data movement overlaps with compute.

items.title: Efficient Memory Management for Large Language Model Serving with PagedAttention
items.why: Applies paging/virtual-memory ideas to KV-cache management and LLM serving.
items.exercise: Simulate KV blocks, fragmentation and sharing in a tiny allocator.

items.title: Fast Inference from Transformers via Speculative Decoding
items.why: Exact-decoding speedup via a cheap draft model and verification by the target model.
items.exercise: Implement draft-then-verify decoding on a toy autoregressive model.

items.title: H2O: Heavy-Hitter Oracle for Efficient Generative Inference of Large Language Models
items.why: Representative KV-cache compression/eviction method based on important tokens.
items.exercise: Implement an attention-score-based KV eviction policy.

items.title: SmoothQuant: Accurate and Efficient Post-Training Quantization for Large Language Models
items.why: Hardware-friendly W8A8 quantization by moving activation outlier difficulty into weights.
items.exercise: Implement the equivalent scaling transform and inspect ranges.

items.title: GPTQ: Accurate Post-Training Quantization for Generative Pre-trained Transformers
items.why: Influential second-order post-training weight quantization for very large Transformers.
items.exercise: Work through the approximate-Hessian idea on a small linear layer.

items.title: AWQ: Activation-aware Weight Quantization for LLM Compression and Acceleration
items.why: Practical low-bit weight-only quantization using activation-aware salient channels.
items.exercise: Use activation stats to identify/protect salient channels.

items.title: Retrieval-Augmented Generation for Knowledge-Intensive NLP Tasks
items.why: Foundational retrieval-augmented generation combining parametric and non-parametric memory.
items.exercise: Build a tiny retriever + generator pipeline with provenance.

items.title: Chain-of-Thought Prompting Elicits Reasoning in Large Language Models
items.why: Established intermediate reasoning traces as a powerful prompting technique.
items.exercise: Compare zero-shot/few-shot/CoT accuracy and token cost.

items.title: Self-Consistency Improves Chain of Thought Reasoning in Language Models
items.why: Sample-many-and-vote reasoning; direct precursor to test-time scaling.
items.exercise: Sample multiple reasoning paths and majority-vote answers.

items.title: ReAct: Synergizing Reasoning and Acting in Language Models
items.why: Influential reasoning + action loop for tool-using agents.
items.exercise: Build a reason→tool→observe→answer loop.

items.title: Toolformer: Language Models Can Teach Themselves to Use Tools
items.why: Important bridge from language modeling to learned API/tool use.
items.exercise: Generate synthetic API-call examples and train a tiny selector.

items.title: Tree of Thoughts: Deliberate Problem Solving with Large Language Models
items.why: Extends CoT into explicit search over candidate reasoning states.
items.exercise: Implement breadth-first search over candidate thoughts.

items.title: Training Verifiers to Solve Math Word Problems
items.why: Key precursor to verifier-guided reasoning and test-time candidate selection; introduces GSM8K.
items.exercise: Train a tiny reranker to choose among generated solutions.

items.title: Let's Verify Step by Step
items.why: Important process-reward-model work comparing step-level vs outcome supervision.
items.exercise: Create step-level correctness labels and train a toy scorer.

items.title: DeepSeekMath: Pushing the Limits of Mathematical Reasoning in Open Language Models
items.why: Introduces GRPO; key bridge into modern RL-based reasoning models.
items.exercise: Derive GRPO and implement group-relative advantages on toy rewards.

items.title: Scaling LLM Test-Time Compute Optimally can be More Effective than Scaling Model Parameters
items.why: Studies how to allocate extra inference compute and when it can beat scaling the base model.
items.exercise: Compare best-of-N, verifier selection and adaptive compute.

items.title: s1: Simple test-time scaling
items.why: Concrete minimal recipe for test-time scaling using budget forcing and a small curated set.
items.exercise: Reproduce budget-forcing behavior and plot accuracy vs tokens.

items.title: Switch Transformers: Scaling to Trillion Parameter Models with Simple and Efficient Sparsity
items.why: Foundational sparse-MoE paper: top-1 routing, capacity, stability and communication.
items.exercise: Implement a top-1 router with expert capacity limits.

items.title: DeepSeekMoE: Towards Ultimate Expert Specialization in Mixture-of-Experts Language Models
items.why: Finer-grained routed experts plus shared experts for specialization and efficiency.
items.exercise: Implement shared+routed experts and inspect load balance.

items.title: DeepSeek-V2: A Strong, Economical, and Efficient Mixture-of-Experts Language Model
items.why: Essential for MLA, compressed KV representation and modern MoE design.
items.exercise: Derive MLA cache math and compare memory with MHA/GQA.

items.title: DeepSeek-V3 Technical Report
items.why: Modern MoE training report: FP8, load balancing, multi-token prediction and communication efficiency.
items.exercise: Create a systems map of precision, routing, parallelism and communication.

items.title: DeepSeek-R1: Incentivizing Reasoning Capability in LLMs via Reinforcement Learning
items.why: Central modern reasoning-RL paper connecting GRPO-style RL, SFT and distillation.
items.exercise: Map the R1 training stages and compare RL-only/SFT+RL/distillation.

items.title: Mamba: Linear-Time Sequence Modeling with Selective State Spaces
items.why: Best-known selective state-space alternative to attention with hardware-aware recurrent execution.
items.exercise: Implement a tiny selective SSM and compare sequence scaling with attention.

items.title: Muon is Scalable for LLM Training
items.why: Newer matrix-orthogonalization optimizer direction; interesting but less settled than core foundations.
items.exercise: Implement matrix orthogonalization on small weights and compare updates with AdamW.

collections.title: Computer Vision, SAR & Earth Observation
collections.subtitle: Vision foundations, SSL, registration, multimodal EO, SAR physics, forecasting

items.title: ImageNet Classification with Deep Convolutional Neural Networks
items.why: Historical CNN turning point; read mainly to understand how modern vision evolved.
items.exercise: Rebuild a tiny AlexNet-style classifier and compare with a residual network.

items.title: Deep Residual Learning for Image Recognition
items.why: Residual connections remain fundamental across vision and many EO backbones.
items.exercise: Implement a residual block; compare trainability of plain vs residual deep CNNs.

items.title: U-Net: Convolutional Networks for Biomedical Image Segmentation
items.why: Encoder-decoder with skip connections is still a superb baseline for segmentation and raster-to-raster prediction.
items.exercise: Train U-Net on a small segmentation task; inspect boundary and scale failures.

items.title: Faster R-CNN: Towards Real-Time Object Detection with Region Proposal Networks
items.why: Foundational two-stage detector; useful for understanding object detection in satellite imagery.
items.exercise: Train/inspect a small detector and learn IoU, anchors/proposals and NMS.

items.title: Feature Pyramid Networks for Object Detection
items.why: Multi-scale features matter enormously in remote sensing where target sizes vary sharply.
items.exercise: Add an FPN to a backbone and inspect performance by object scale.

items.title: End-to-End Object Detection with Transformers
items.why: Shows set prediction and Transformer-based detection without hand-designed NMS pipelines.
items.exercise: Understand bipartite matching loss; fine-tune a lightweight DETR variant.

items.title: An Image is Worth 16x16 Words: Transformers for Image Recognition at Scale
items.why: Critical bridge from Transformer concepts to patch-based vision; foundation for many EO models.
items.exercise: Implement patch embedding + ViT encoder and visualize attention/patch effects.

items.title: Swin Transformer: Hierarchical Vision Transformer using Shifted Windows
items.why: Hierarchical local-window attention is highly relevant for large remote-sensing images and dense prediction.
items.exercise: Compare global ViT attention cost with shifted-window attention at increasing image sizes.

items.title: SegFormer: Simple and Efficient Design for Semantic Segmentation with Transformers
items.why: Strong, relatively simple Transformer segmentation architecture; useful EO baseline.
items.exercise: Fine-tune SegFormer on a small land-cover/flood segmentation dataset.

items.title: Masked-attention Mask Transformer for Universal Image Segmentation
items.why: Modern unification of semantic, instance and panoptic segmentation.
items.exercise: Study mask classification and compare with pixel-wise segmentation objectives.

items.title: A Simple Framework for Contrastive Learning of Visual Representations
items.why: Foundational contrastive SSL recipe; useful when EO labels are scarce.
items.exercise: Pretrain with contrastive augmentations, then linear-probe vs supervised-from-scratch.

items.title: Emerging Properties in Self-Supervised Vision Transformers
items.why: Shows powerful self-distilled ViT representations and emergent spatial structure without labels.
items.exercise: Run DINO features on EO patches and visualize nearest neighbors/attention maps.

items.title: Masked Autoencoders Are Scalable Vision Learners
items.why: Masked image modeling is central to modern geospatial foundation models.
items.exercise: Implement a tiny masked-image reconstruction objective and compare masking ratios.

items.title: DINOv2: Learning Robust Visual Features without Supervision
items.why: High-quality general visual features; useful benchmark against domain-specific EO encoders.
items.exercise: Extract frozen DINOv2 features for SAR/optical downstream tasks as a transfer baseline.

items.title: Segment Anything
items.why: Promptable segmentation foundation model; useful to understand zero/few-shot segmentation and annotation assistance.
items.exercise: Test SAM on optical/SAR imagery and document domain-shift failure modes.

items.title: Learning Transferable Visual Models From Natural Language Supervision
items.why: Core vision-language pretraining idea needed to understand RemoteCLIP and semantic zero-shot transfer.
items.exercise: Try zero-shot classification and compare generic CLIP with RemoteCLIP later.

items.title: SuperPoint: Self-Supervised Interest Point Detection and Description
items.why: Learned keypoints/descriptors are a natural benchmark against handcrafted registration features.
items.exercise: Match two transformed images; measure repeatability and homography error.

items.title: SuperGlue: Learning Feature Matching with Graph Neural Networks
items.why: Adds context-aware matching over sparse local features; strong reference for geometric correspondence.
items.exercise: Pair SuperPoint + SuperGlue; evaluate match precision under viewpoint/radiometric changes.

items.title: LoFTR: Detector-Free Local Feature Matching with Transformers
items.why: Dense coarse-to-fine matching can work in low-texture areas where keypoint detectors struggle; highly relevant to multi-sensor registration.
items.exercise: Benchmark LoFTR on manually verified SAR/optical or temporal image pairs and inspect outliers.

items.title: LightGlue: Local Feature Matching at Light Speed
items.why: Modern efficient sparse matcher with adaptive computation; useful for practical registration pipelines.
items.exercise: Compare LightGlue vs SuperGlue speed/accuracy on easy and difficult pairs.

items.title: RAFT: Recurrent All-Pairs Field Transforms for Optical Flow
items.why: Dense correspondence/flow ideas are useful when registration includes local warps rather than a global translation.
items.exercise: Run RAFT on synthetic warps; inspect whether flow fields recover known displacement.

items.title: AROSICS: An Automated and Robust Open-Source Image Co-Registration Software for Multi-Sensor Satellite Data
items.why: Directly relevant: sub-pixel multi-sensor satellite co-registration using phase correlation, tie-point grids and quality filtering.
items.exercise: Use AROSICS as a baseline; log local/global shifts, tie-point acceptance and post-registration residuals.

items.title: BigEarthNet: A Large-Scale Benchmark Archive for Remote Sensing Image Understanding
items.why: Large EO benchmark useful for land-cover representation learning and transfer.
items.exercise: Use a small subset for a consistent optical pretraining/evaluation baseline.

items.title: SEN12MS: A Curated Dataset of Georeferenced Multi-Spectral Sentinel-1/2 Imagery for Deep Learning and Data Fusion
items.why: Aligned Sentinel-1 SAR + Sentinel-2 optical data is ideal for multimodal fusion experiments.
items.exercise: Train SAR-only, optical-only and fused baselines with exactly the same splits.

items.title: SSL4EO-S12: A Large-Scale Multi-Modal, Multi-Temporal Dataset for Self-Supervised Learning in Earth Observation
items.why: Global Sentinel-1/2 multimodal, multitemporal corpus designed for SSL; excellent bridge from generic SSL to EO.
items.exercise: Pretrain or use released encoders; compare transfer on one SAR-heavy downstream task.

items.title: SatMAE: Pre-training Transformers for Temporal and Multi-Spectral Satellite Imagery
items.why: Adapts masked autoencoding to multispectral and temporal satellite inputs.
items.exercise: Reproduce a small temporal/multispectral masking experiment and compare with RGB-style MAE.

items.title: Rethinking Transformers Pre-training for Multi-Spectral Satellite Imagery (SatMAE++)
items.why: Extends satellite masked modeling toward stronger spatial/spectral representation learning.
items.exercise: Study which spectral/spatial masking choices transfer best to your sensor mix.

items.title: CROMA: Remote Sensing Representations with Contrastive Radar-Optical Masked Autoencoders
items.why: One of the most directly useful papers for aligned radar-optical representation learning: contrastive + masked reconstruction + fusion.
items.exercise: Use CROMA embeddings for cross-sensor matching or downstream classification; test sensitivity to misregistration.

items.title: Foundation Models for Generalist Geospatial Artificial Intelligence
items.why: Important geospatial FM blueprint with multi-temporal HLS pretraining and varied downstream tasks.
items.exercise: Fine-tune released Prithvi features on one segmentation or temporal imputation task.

items.title: Neural Plasticity-Inspired Multimodal Foundation Model for Earth Observation
items.why: Dynamic sensor-aware processing across heterogeneous EO modalities; very relevant to multi-mission thinking.
items.exercise: Study the dynamic wavelength/sensor conditioning idea and design an analogous metadata-conditioning block for SAR.

items.title: AnySat: An Earth Observation Model for Any Resolutions, Scales, and Modalities
items.why: Unified self-supervised model for heterogeneous sensors/resolutions/scales; directly relevant to cross-mission EO representation learning.
items.exercise: Map ALOS/NISAR/Sentinel inputs into its modality/resolution design assumptions and identify gaps.

items.title: Galileo: Learning Global and Local Features in Pretrained Remote Sensing Models
items.why: Flexible multimodal EO pretraining with explicit global/local feature objectives; useful for varying spatial and temporal scales.
items.exercise: Compare global-vs-local feature objectives on one patch-level and one pixel-level task.

items.title: RemoteCLIP: A Vision Language Foundation Model for Remote Sensing
items.why: Adds language-aligned semantics to remote-sensing representations; useful for retrieval, zero-shot tagging and dataset exploration.
items.exercise: Compare CLIP vs RemoteCLIP embeddings on EO retrieval or scene classification.

items.title: SAR2SAR: A Semi-Supervised Despeckling Algorithm for SAR Images
items.why: Practical learning-based SAR despeckling that respects the difficulty of obtaining clean SAR targets.
items.exercise: Implement/evaluate on simulated speckle first, then inspect real-data texture preservation.

items.title: As if by magic: self-supervised training of deep despeckling networks with MERLIN
items.why: Self-supervised SAR despeckling avoids clean reference targets and is a strong example of using SAR statistics in learning.
items.exercise: Compare MERLIN-style self-supervision with naive supervised synthetic-speckle training.

items.title: A Survey of Complex-Valued Neural Networks
items.why: Complex-valued networks matter when amplitude and phase are both meaningful rather than collapsing SAR to intensity images.
items.exercise: Implement a small complex linear/convolution layer and verify complex gradients numerically.

items.title: SARFormer: An Acquisition Parameter Aware Vision Transformer for Synthetic Aperture Radar Data
items.why: Directly relevant to acquisition-aware SAR modeling: inject geometry/acquisition parameters rather than treating SAR as ordinary imagery.
items.exercise: Reproduce the conditioning idea with incidence angle / orbit / polarization metadata on a small task.

items.title: A Complex-valued SAR Foundation Model Based on Physically Inspired Representation Learning
items.why: Combines complex SAR, physical scattering ideas and self-supervised foundation-model learning; excellent physics-aware direction.
items.exercise: Study scattering-query supervision and identify which parts are usable with your available complex products.

items.title: Convolutional LSTM Network: A Machine Learning Approach for Precipitation Nowcasting
items.why: Canonical spatiotemporal forecasting baseline; still worth having before jumping to Transformers.
items.exercise: Use ConvLSTM as a strict baseline for T-k → T+1 satellite prediction.

items.title: PredRNN: A Recurrent Neural Network for Spatiotemporal Predictive Learning
items.why: Models deep-in-time spatial dynamics and gives a stronger recurrent baseline than plain ConvLSTM.
items.exercise: Benchmark PredRNN against ConvLSTM on identical temporal windows and loss functions.

items.title: SimVP: Simpler yet Better Video Prediction
items.why: Excellent simple baseline: separates spatial encoder/decoder from temporal translator without recurrent complexity.
items.exercise: Make SimVP your 'must beat' baseline before complex temporal architectures.

items.title: Earthformer: Exploring Space-Time Transformers for Earth System Forecasting
items.why: Space-time Transformer specifically motivated by Earth-system forecasting; highly relevant to structured EO sequences.
items.exercise: Adapt cuboid attention ideas to your temporal SAR patches and compare memory/accuracy to SimVP.

items.title: Disentangling Physical Dynamics from Unknown Factors for Unsupervised Video Prediction
items.why: Useful physics-aware forecasting idea: explicitly separate physical dynamics from residual/unknown components.
items.exercise: Design a two-stream predictor: constrained physical component + learned residual component.

items.title: Physics Informed Deep Learning (Part I): Data-driven Solutions of Nonlinear Partial Differential Equations
items.why: Foundational physics-informed neural-network formulation; not SAR-specific, but teaches how equations can become learning constraints.
items.exercise: Implement a toy PINN, then write down which SAR/geometry constraints are equations vs metadata vs invariances.

items.title: Physics-informed machine learning
items.why: Broader and more useful than PINNs alone: surveys ways to encode physics through losses, architectures, hybrid models and priors.
items.exercise: Classify your planned SAR constraints as observational, inductive, learning-bias or hybrid-model constraints.

collections.title: Regulated AI: Law & Banking
collections.subtitle: Domain data, evaluation, uncertainty, privacy, governance, operational controls

items.title: LEGAL-BERT: The Muppets straight out of Law School
items.why: Best starting point for understanding domain-adaptive pretraining in legal NLP and why generic-language recipes do not always transfer cleanly.
items.exercise: Fine-tune generic BERT vs LEGAL-BERT on the same small legal classification task and compare calibration + error types.

items.title: When Does Pretraining Help? Assessing Self-Supervised Learning for Law and the CaseHOLD Dataset
items.why: A legally meaningful case-law benchmark built around identifying holdings; good bridge from domain pretraining to reasoning-style evaluation.
items.exercise: Reproduce a CaseHOLD baseline, then inspect failures by citation context length and legal vocabulary.

items.title: CUAD: An Expert-Annotated NLP Dataset for Legal Contract Review
items.why: Expert-labelled contract review dataset; directly relevant to clause extraction, evidence spans and human-in-the-loop legal review.
items.exercise: Build clause retrieval/extraction with evidence spans and an explicit 'no evidence' outcome.

items.title: ContractNLI: A Dataset for Document-level Natural Language Inference for Contracts
items.why: Excellent regulated-domain formulation: entailment, contradiction, neutral and evidence identification over long contracts.
items.exercise: Implement chunked long-document NLI; score both label accuracy and evidence-span quality.

items.title: Pile of Law: Learning Responsible Data Filtering from the Law and a 256GB Open-Source Legal Dataset
items.why: Combines legal-domain corpus construction with privacy, toxicity and responsible data-filtering questions.
items.exercise: Create a mini datasheet for a legal corpus and define inclusion/exclusion rules with provenance.

items.title: LexGLUE: A Benchmark Dataset for Legal Language Understanding in English
items.why: Standardized legal NLU benchmark spanning several task families; useful for learning how to evaluate across legal subdomains rather than one task.
items.exercise: Run two model families on two LexGLUE tasks and report macro/micro metrics plus per-class errors.

items.title: LeXFiles and LegalLAMA: Facilitating English Multinational Legal Language Model Development
items.why: Useful for multinational legal corpora, knowledge probing and separating upstream language knowledge from downstream task performance.
items.exercise: Design a tiny Singapore-law probing set: statutes, court names, citation forms and doctrinal concepts.

items.title: LegalBench: A Collaboratively Built Benchmark for Measuring Legal Reasoning in Large Language Models
items.why: A broad legal-reasoning benchmark built with legal experts; crucial for thinking beyond generic QA accuracy.
items.exercise: Select 8-12 task types and build an evaluation harness with exact-match, abstention and evidence checks.

items.title: LawBench: Benchmarking Legal Knowledge of Large Language Models
items.why: Separates memorization, understanding and application of legal knowledge; useful mental model even if the jurisdiction differs.
items.exercise: Map your own legal tasks into memorization / understanding / application and create held-out tests for each.

items.title: LexGenius: An Expert-Level Benchmark for Large Language Models in Legal General Intelligence
items.why: Recent expert-level legal benchmark; valuable for benchmark design, freshness and leakage-aware evaluation even though it is Chinese-law focused.
items.exercise: Study its task taxonomy and adapt only the evaluation-design ideas to your jurisdiction.

items.title: FinBERT: Financial Sentiment Analysis with Pre-trained Language Models
items.why: Classic example of domain adaptation in finance; simple enough to reproduce and useful for learning domain shift.
items.exercise: Benchmark generic BERT vs FinBERT on financial sentiment and analyze errors around negation and forward-looking language.

items.title: FiNER: Financial Numeric Entity Recognition for XBRL Tagging
items.why: Shows why numeric expressions and financial filings need special handling; also introduces SEC-BERT.
items.exercise: Build a numeric-entity tagger and compare raw numbers vs normalized/pseudo-token representations.

items.title: FinQA: A Dataset of Numerical Reasoning over Financial Data
items.why: Excellent benchmark for multi-step numerical reasoning over text + tables with executable reasoning programs.
items.exercise: Build retrieval + program generation; verify arithmetic by execution rather than trusting free-form text.

items.title: ConvFinQA: Exploring the Chain of Numerical Reasoning in Conversational Finance Question Answering
items.why: Adds conversational context and long-range numerical dependencies to finance QA.
items.exercise: Create a conversation-state representation and compare single-turn vs multi-turn reasoning errors.

items.title: FinanceBench: A New Benchmark for Financial Question Answering
items.why: Open-book financial QA benchmark with evidence strings; especially useful for enterprise RAG evaluation and hallucination analysis.
items.exercise: Build citation-grounded QA with answer, evidence, abstention, retrieval recall and numerical-verification metrics.

items.title: BloombergGPT: A Large Language Model for Finance
items.why: A useful study of mixed general + proprietary financial corpora, tokenizer choices and domain/general capability trade-offs.
items.exercise: Compare its data mixture and evaluation design to a generic LLM report; write a domain-model design memo.

items.title: Why Should I Trust You?: Explaining the Predictions of Any Classifier
items.why: Foundational local explanation method; regulated work requires understanding what an explanation can and cannot establish.
items.exercise: Explain the same predictions with LIME under multiple perturbation settings and test stability.

items.title: A Unified Approach to Interpreting Model Predictions
items.why: Shapley-based explanation framework widely used in model-risk and high-stakes analytics.
items.exercise: Compute SHAP for a tabular credit-risk toy model and compare global vs local explanations.

items.title: On Calibration of Modern Neural Networks
items.why: In regulated decisions, a calibrated probability can be more useful than raw accuracy; temperature scaling is a practical baseline.
items.exercise: Plot reliability diagrams/ECE before and after temperature scaling.

items.title: A Gentle Introduction to Conformal Prediction and Distribution-Free Uncertainty Quantification
items.why: Gives set-valued predictions with finite-sample coverage guarantees under assumptions; powerful for uncertainty-aware workflows.
items.exercise: Implement split conformal classification and measure empirical coverage vs set size.

items.title: SelectiveNet: A Deep Neural Network with an Integrated Reject Option
items.why: Formalizes abstention/rejection, a key design pattern when a model should hand uncertain cases to humans.
items.exercise: Create a risk-coverage curve and choose an operating point for human escalation.

items.title: Model Cards for Model Reporting
items.why: A practical template for communicating intended use, limitations and subgroup performance.
items.exercise: Write a model card for one of your own models including failure modes and human-oversight boundaries.

items.title: Datasheets for Datasets
items.why: Data provenance and fitness-for-purpose are central in law and banking; this gives a rigorous documentation structure.
items.exercise: Produce a datasheet for a legal/financial dataset with collection, licensing, exclusions and known skews.

items.title: Equality of Opportunity in Supervised Learning
items.why: A foundational fairness formulation; useful for learning the tension between error rates, protected groups and operational thresholds.
items.exercise: Measure equalized-odds gaps on a toy lending model and study threshold trade-offs.

items.title: Counterfactual Fairness
items.why: Introduces a causal view of fairness, useful when correlation-only fairness metrics are insufficient.
items.exercise: Draw a causal graph for a lending or legal triage task and identify impermissible paths.

items.title: Membership Inference Attacks Against Machine Learning Models
items.why: Shows that models can leak whether examples were in training data; directly relevant to confidential records and personal data.
items.exercise: Run a small membership-inference experiment and document mitigations.

items.title: Extracting Training Data from Large Language Models
items.why: Demonstrates memorization/privacy leakage from generative models; essential for sensitive corpora.
items.exercise: Create canary strings in a toy LM and measure memorization/extraction risk.

items.title: Artificial Intelligence Risk Management Framework (AI RMF 1.0)
items.why: A practical, use-case-agnostic risk-management framework; good backbone for translating technical evaluation into governance.
items.exercise: Map one AI system to Govern / Map / Measure / Manage and create an evidence checklist.

items.title: Artificial Intelligence Risk Management Framework: Generative Artificial Intelligence Profile (NIST AI 600-1)
items.why: Extends AI RMF with GenAI-specific risks and actions; highly practical for RAG, assistants and generative workflows.
items.exercise: Turn the profile into testable controls for a domain RAG application.

items.title: Model AI Governance Framework for Generative AI
items.why: Singapore-specific governance framing for generative AI; useful for deployment decisions, accountability and safety evaluation.
items.exercise: Create a one-page mapping from its governance dimensions to concrete engineering controls.

items.title: Model AI Governance Framework for Agentic AI
items.why: Current Singapore framework for bounded autonomy, human checkpoints, tool/data access and agent lifecycle controls.
items.exercise: Define an agent permission model: allowed tools, approval checkpoints, audit log and kill switch.

items.title: Advisory Guidelines on use of Personal Data in AI Recommendation and Decision Systems
items.why: Directly connects AI development/deployment to Singapore personal-data obligations and good practices.
items.exercise: Create a data-flow diagram and tag collection, training, testing, inference and logging data with PDPA obligations.

items.title: AI Verify / AI Verify Toolkit
items.why: Turns responsible-AI principles into technical tests; current toolkit also supports sector extensions such as finance.
items.exercise: Run a small model through available tests and save an evidence pack alongside model/data documentation.

items.title: FEAT Principles and Veritas Toolkit
items.why: Singapore finance-specific fairness, ethics, accountability and transparency framework, with testing support through Veritas/AIVT.
items.exercise: Map a credit-risk or fraud model to FEAT and define quantitative fairness + explainability evidence.

items.title: MAS Technology Risk Management: Notice / FAQs and related guidance
items.why: AI systems in financial institutions live inside broader technology-risk, resilience, access-control and third-party-risk obligations.
items.exercise: Create a dependency and control inventory for an AI service, including model vendor, cloud, data and monitoring dependencies.

items.title: The Financial Stability Implications of Artificial Intelligence
items.why: Broad financial-system view of AI vulnerabilities including third-party concentration, cyber, model risk and data governance.
items.exercise: Make a risk register separating model-level, firm-level and ecosystem-level risks.

items.title: Sound Practices for Responsible Adoption of Artificial Intelligence
items.why: Very current practical guidance for organization-wide AI governance and lifecycle risk management in financial institutions.
items.exercise: Turn the 12 practices into a maturity checklist and score a hypothetical bank AI deployment.

items.title: Regulation (EU) 2024/1689 – Artificial Intelligence Act
items.why: Important risk-based regulatory reference for organizations operating in or serving the EU; useful for understanding legal obligations around high-risk AI.
items.exercise: Classify 5 example systems by likely risk category and identify documentation/human-oversight implications.

collections.title: Books, Courses & Tutorials
collections.subtitle: Math refresh, DL core, vision, GPU systems, SAR/EO, trustworthy AI

items.title: Mathematics for Machine Learning
items.why: Compact linear algebra, matrix decompositions, calculus, probability and optimization specifically for ML.
items.exercise: Do Ch. 2, 4, 5, 6, 7 first; solve selected exercises and implement decompositions/gradients in NumPy.

items.title: Probabilistic Machine Learning: An Introduction
items.why: Modern probabilistic treatment with code and exercises; excellent for uncertainty, Bayesian thinking and statistical ML.
items.exercise: Prioritize probability, decision theory, linear/logistic regression, kernels, latent variables and deep learning chapters as needed.

items.title: Probabilistic Machine Learning: Advanced Topics
items.why: Strong reference for variational inference, graphical models, Bayesian deep learning and advanced uncertainty.
items.exercise: Do not read cover-to-cover now. Pull chapters when a research problem demands them.

items.title: Understanding Deep Learning
items.why: Probably the best single modern DL textbook for a mathematically capable engineer: concise, visual and current through Transformers/diffusion.
items.exercise: Read in order and complete the Python notebooks for backprop, convnets, attention, Transformers and generative models.

items.title: Deep Learning
items.why: Still a foundational reference for optimization, regularization, representation learning and generative modeling.
items.exercise: Use as a theory reference rather than a primary 2026 course. Deep-read numerical computation, optimization and regularization when needed.

items.title: Dive into Deep Learning
items.why: Executable notebooks combine math, code and experiments; excellent for implementation fluency.
items.exercise: Use PyTorch chapters to implement linear models, MLPs, CNNs, attention/Transformers and training tricks.

items.title: Neural Networks: Zero to Hero
items.why: One of the best from-scratch coding explanations of backprop, MLPs, language modeling and GPT construction.
items.exercise: Code every lecture, do the exercises, and avoid passive watching.

items.title: MIT 6.S191 Introduction to Deep Learning
items.why: Fast, high-quality refresher across modern deep learning with lecture videos and practical framing.
items.exercise: Watch the core lectures and implement one lab; use it as consolidation, not your only DL course.

items.shortName: Computer Vision: Algorithms and Applications, 2nd ed.
items.title: Computer Vision: Algorithms and Applications, 2nd ed.
items.why: Outstanding bridge between classical geometry/image processing and modern vision; especially valuable before registration work.
items.exercise: Prioritize image formation, filtering, features/matching, alignment, motion, recognition and computational photography sections.

items.shortName: CS231n: Deep Learning for Computer Vision
items.title: CS231n: Deep Learning for Computer Vision
items.why: Deep, assignment-driven modern vision curriculum from fundamentals through Transformers, SSL, diffusion and distributed training.
items.exercise: Do the lecture sequence and at least the key coding assignments on backprop/CNNs plus one modern-vision assignment.

items.title: MIT 6.7960 Deep Learning
items.why: More advanced modern DL course; useful once core foundations are comfortable.
items.exercise: Select lectures on optimization, generative modeling, representation learning and vision based on current work.

items.shortName: Programming Massively Parallel Processors: A Hands-on Approach
items.title: Programming Massively Parallel Processors: A Hands-on Approach
items.why: The book to pair with GPU MODE: architecture, memory locality, reductions, scans, convolution, sparse work and performance reasoning.
items.exercise: Code chapters 2-10 in CUDA; benchmark each optimization and write down bandwidth/FLOP bottlenecks.

items.title: GPU MODE / CUDA MODE Lectures
items.why: Current practitioner-level material on profiling, CUDA, memory, quantization, Triton, compilers and production kernels.
items.exercise: Start with lectures 1-9; reproduce profiling, memory and reduction exercises before jumping to newer compiler topics.

items.title: Full Stack Deep Learning
items.why: Covers the parts research courses often miss: testing, data, deployment, monitoring, continual learning and project structure.
items.exercise: Complete troubleshooting/testing, data management, deployment and monitoring lectures/labs.

items.title: Designing Machine Learning Systems
items.why: Excellent systems-design perspective on data, metrics, deployment, monitoring and continual updates.
items.exercise: Read with one real system in mind; create a design doc that identifies data/serving/monitoring failure modes.

items.title: Understanding Synthetic Aperture Radar Images
items.why: Classic deep reference for SAR image formation, statistics, filtering, parameter estimation and interpretation.
items.exercise: Read slowly alongside actual SAR products; keep a notebook of image phenomena, assumptions and equations.

items.shortName: Synthetic Aperture Radar Signal Processing with MATLAB Algorithms
items.title: Synthetic Aperture Radar Signal Processing with MATLAB Algorithms
items.why: Strong signal-processing treatment of SAR acquisition and wavefront reconstruction with implementation-oriented algorithms.
items.exercise: Work through range/azimuth concepts and reproduce selected companion algorithms, translating to Python where useful.

items.shortName: Deep Learning for the Earth Sciences
items.title: Deep Learning for the Earth Sciences
items.why: Rare book connecting deep learning, remote sensing, forecasting, co-registration, fusion and physics-aware modeling.
items.exercise: Prioritize segmentation, fusion/matching/co-registration, forecasting/interpolation and physics-aware chapters.

items.shortName: NASA ARSET: An Introduction to SAR and Its Applications
items.title: NASA ARSET: An Introduction to SAR and Its Applications
items.why: Current, authoritative practical SAR introduction that covers signal-surface interaction, interpretation and sensor capabilities.
items.exercise: Watch all parts and reproduce the interpretation examples on your own Sentinel-1/NISAR scenes.

items.shortName: NASA ARSET: Basics of Synthetic Aperture Radar (4 sessions)
items.title: NASA ARSET: Basics of Synthetic Aperture Radar (4 sessions)
items.why: Very approachable coverage of image interpretation, distortions, polarimetry and interferometry.
items.exercise: Use as a visual refresher, then make a one-page cheat sheet of geometry, layover/shadow, polarization and InSAR.

items.title: NISAR SAR Education Resources
items.why: Curated gateway to ASF tutorials, SAR Semester, UNAVCO, ARSET and NISAR-oriented material.
items.exercise: Use this as your authoritative index; pick tutorials only when they serve a current prototype need.

items.title: EO College SAR Resources
items.why: Broad collection covering SAR basics, processing, polarimetry, interferometry, estimation and mission-specific material.
items.exercise: Do Basics of SAR, SAR processing/data analysis, then InSAR/polarimetry modules as relevant.

items.title: ESA/CONAE L/C/X-band SAR Training Course
items.why: Theory and practicals across L/C/X-band SAR, including exercises with Sentinel-1 and ALOS/PALSAR-2.
items.exercise: Do the vegetation, InSAR or polarimetry practical that best matches your current data.

items.title: Interpretable Machine Learning
items.why: Excellent practical and critical guide to explanation methods; the 2025 edition is current and freely readable online.
items.exercise: Implement permutation importance, PDP/ALE and SHAP; explicitly document when each explanation can mislead.

items.title: Artificial Intelligence and Legal Analytics
items.why: Gives historical and conceptual depth on computational legal reasoning, prediction, argument and text analytics beyond today's LLM framing.
items.exercise: Prioritize statutory reasoning, case-based reasoning, legal outcome prediction and legal text analytics chapters.

items.shortName: CS224N: Natural Language Processing with Deep Learning
items.title: CS224N: Natural Language Processing with Deep Learning
items.why: Strong modern NLP course with Transformers, practical projects, agents/RAG and benchmarking/evaluation material.
items.exercise: Prioritize Transformers, final-project/practical tips, benchmarking/evaluation and domain-relevant assignments.

items.title: Practical Deep Learning for Coders
items.why: Fast route through applying deep learning and building intuition; especially useful when you want to ship a quick baseline.
items.exercise: Do only the lessons that fill gaps; avoid duplicating topics already mastered through DeepML/other courses.
